title: Epsilon Indi B — a pair of nearby brown dwarfs
plain_result: From SPHEREx pictures alone we measured how fast it moves across the sky: +3.96 ± 0.07″ and -2.43 ± 0.07″ per year (east–west, north–south). ESA's Gaia measured +3.98″ and -2.47″.
method_note: Each picture is fitted with the star's position free, saturated pixels masked and Gaia neighbours modelled; the motion is a straight-line fit to SPHEREx positions alone with Gaia's parallax held fixed. Positions sit a steady ~0.5″ south of Gaia's prediction in every survey; the pair is unresolved, so a shifted centre of light is possible — not explained here.
